clue.text: Crush a dignitary

parts.note: a pash is British schoolgirl slang for a crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: Someone is told to squash an important official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a verb to squash, but here it is the noun: PASH is old British slang for an infatuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking official in the Ottoman Empire, so a title for a grandee.

clue.text: Overworks animal — tame one burrowing into the Spanish mountain

parts.note: read as over plus works: works are OP OP (two op. abbreviations for musical works), turned over to read backwards
a cat is an animal

indicators.note: burrowing into puts the pet inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a pet is a tame animal

explanation.surface: Someone overworks an animal, while a tame creature digs into a Spanish peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overworks' looks like one verb, but splits as 'Over' (turn back) and 'works', OP OP, giving POPO. The answer is a volcano in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Popocatépetl is an active volcanic mountain near Mexico City.

clue.text: Smutty stuff on the royal family's fabulous afterbirth

parts.note: soot is the black smut left by burning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
kin means family

explanation.surface: Something dirty is said about the royal family's legendary birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smutty' suggests rude, but means sooty. 'fabulous' means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sooterkin was a mythical afterbirth, a mouse-like creature Dutch women were fabled to bear.

clue.text: Ex-boxer catches Zeus's lover dressing

indicators.note: catches means holds, so the boxer wraps round the lover

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous former heavyweight champion
Io was a mortal loved by Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A retired fighter traps a mythical woman getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests putting on clothes, but it is a sauce for salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise used as a dressing or dip.

clue.text: Mowlam on horseback — turncoat and rabble-rouser

parts.note: Mo Mowlam was a British Labour cabinet minister, known as Mo
a cob is a sturdy horse; back tells us to read the word cob backwards
a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: A politician rides a horse while being called a traitor and agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was Northern Ireland Secretary in the late 1990s. 'horseback' is horse plus back: the horse word read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobocrat is a leader or champion of mob rule, one who stirs up the crowd.

clue.text: Transport for emigrants is a potential bloomer

definitions.meaning: the ship that carried the Pilgrim settlers to America in 1620
a flower that may bloom: read as may plus flower

explanation.surface: A ship carrying emigrants is a flower waiting to bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a flower that 'may' bloom is only potentially a bloomer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers sailed on the Mayflower, and a mayflower is also a plant blooming in May.

clue.text: Rugby team's memory

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the rugby team has the letters inside its words

explanation.surface: A rugby side's recollection.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'rugBY TEam'.
explanation.definitionFit: A byte is a unit of computer memory, eight bits.

clue.text: Woman torn apart by aristocrat's disaster

indicators.note: torn apart by means split open with something forced in, so the aristocrat goes inside the name

parts.note: Cheryl is a woman's name
a nob is a toff, a member of the upper class

explanation.surface: A woman is ripped to pieces by a noble's catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn apart by' looks like violence to the woman, but simply means her name is split open to take the toff.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1986 nuclear accident at the Ukrainian plant of this name was a byword for disaster.

clue.text: A truth universally acknowledged at 10.10 in the morning

indicators.note: in places the two tens inside the abbreviation for the morning

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
ten once as Roman X, then 10 written as letters looking like I and O

explanation.surface: Austen's famous opening is pinned to ten past ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows the first line of Pride and Prejudice. The first 10 is Roman X; the second 10 is read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true by everyone, needing no proof.

clue.text: How plants grow flowers? Keeping warm, new doctoral research reveals

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the bunch of flowers wraps round the word for warm

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers
hot is a stronger synonym of warm
a doctoral candidate's research is written up as a thesis

explanation.surface: A doctoral study reveals how flowers grow when kept warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' tempts as a definition near 'plants', but it is the bunch that 'Keeping' wraps round the warm word.
explanation.definitionFit: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight to make the sugars they live and grow on.

clue.text: Philosopher — to wit, Hungary's first player taking gold after end of match

parts.note: sc., scilicet, means namely or to wit

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Hungary
taking means holding inside, so the batsman takes in the end letter and the gold

parts.note: an opener is a cricketer who opens the batting

indicators.note: after places the gold symbol following the end of match
the end of match is its last letter

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A thinker who is a top Hungarian sportsman wins gold at the end of the match.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is short for scilicet, 'to wit'. 'player' is an OPENER, a batsman in cricket, holding H (end of match) and AU.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Schopenhauer was a German philosopher known for his pessimism.

clue.text: Fabric layer in poor health in church

indicators.note: in places the hen and the illness inside the letters for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a layer is a hen, since it lays eggs
ill means in poor health

explanation.surface: Some cloth is described as a layer in poor health inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' suggests a sheet of fabric, but it is a hen, the bird that lays.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a velvety tufted yarn or the soft cloth woven from it.

clue.text: Coming out elliptical

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of coming are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone's emerging statement is oblique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' reads as a phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on COMING.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliptical speech is terse and hard to follow, as are pithy, aphoristic gnomic sayings.

clue.text: Keep maintaining peak condition and seize the reins

indicators.note: maintaining means holding within, so the castle keep word holds the other letters

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

indicators.note: condition used as a verb means to work into shape, so the letters of peak are reworked

explanation.surface: Keep in top shape and grab control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peak condition' reads as one phrase meaning top form, but 'condition' is the anagram signal working on 'peak' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize the reins is an idiom for taking control, the same as grabbing authority.

clue.text: A scientific figure — pity his science is flawed

indicators.note: is flawed suggests the letters are faulty and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
sc. is an abbreviation for science

explanation.surface: Someone laments that a researcher's science is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is flawed' rearranges PITY, HIS and SC (science).
explanation.definitionFit: A physicist is a scientist working in physics, so a scientific figure.

clue.text: May her swine's flesh putrefy in Yorkshire!

parts.note: to rot is to putrefy
ham is meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: A curse wishing that a woman's pork should go off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a Yorkshire curse; the answer is a town in South Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotherham is a town in South Yorkshire, so a place found in that county.

clue.text: Singer's personal problem involving fool

definitions.note: Singer's here means singer is: the 's links definition and wordplay

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the problem surrounds the fool

parts.note: BO, body odour, is the personal problem of advertising fame
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A vocalist has a hygiene issue that involves an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: BO stands for body odour, the classic 'personal problem' of old British soap adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A basso is a bass singer, the lowest male voice in Italian terminology.

clue.text: Cricket ground's turned small boy into fan of central Europe

indicators.note: turned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: the Oval is a London cricket ground; with the s it gives ovals
Phil is a shortened form of Philip, a boy's name made small

explanation.surface: A cricket ground converted a little lad into a Slav enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a Test cricket ground in south London; OVALS backwards gives SLAVO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slavophil admires Slavic peoples and culture, found across central and eastern Europe.

clue.text: Remuneration Poles received for being anything but macho

indicators.note: received means taken in, so the pay holds the two poles

parts.note: pay is remuneration
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Wages paid to Polish workers for being unmanly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but gives the compass poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pansy is a dated, derogatory term for an effeminate man, the very opposite of a macho one.

clue.text: Terrorists I subsequently sent back come back

indicators.note: sent back tells us the whole run of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Someone says they later dispatched some terrorists, who returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses the whole of ETA+I+LATER. 'come back' is the sense of hitting back, not of returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back at someone can mean to respond in kind, which is retaliation.

clue.text: Very bad habit, taking tabloid

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the habit wraps round the tabloid

parts.note: a tic is a habitual twitch or mannerism
a rag is a disparaging word for a downmarket newspaper

explanation.surface: Reading the tabloids is a terrible habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests a nun's garb, but is a TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, tragic means dreadful or pathetically bad, as in a tragic haircut.

clue.text: Eros reflected on a smell

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the word for love is read backwards

parts.note: Amor is the Roman name of Eros, the god of love

explanation.surface: The love god's image is mirrored on a surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Eros's Roman counterpart AMOR reversed gives ROMA, joined to A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, usually pleasant smell.

clue.text: Drier item for sale aboard train

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the auction item sits inside the word for train

parts.note: to train is to teach
a lot is an item offered for sale at auction

explanation.surface: Goods are on sale aboard a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is a verb, TEACH, not a railway train; 'Drier' is a thing that dries dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cloth is a towel for drying washed dishes, so an item used as a drier.

clue.text: Dog food containers I opened

indicators.note: opened means the containers are opened to take the letter I

parts.note: cans hold food

explanation.surface: Tins of pet food opened by me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog food' reads as one phrase, but 'Dog' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Canis is the Latin genus name for dogs and wolves.

clue.text: Summons jester to entertain the king

indicators.note: to entertain means to hold as a guest, so the jester holds the king

parts.note: a wit is a joker
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A jester is called to amuse the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertain' suggests amusing, but means taking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a written legal order, such as a summons to court.

clue.text: Sanctimonious author in Hamburg's top hotel gets thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the top of Hamburg is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-righteous writer gets ejected from a fine hotel in Hamburg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges AUTHOR, IN, H (the first letter of Hamburg, given by 'top') and HOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sanctimonious acts as if morally superior to everyone else, the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: It's true love! Given the stomach, I'll do anything!

parts.note: a fact is something that is true
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
tum is informal for the stomach

explanation.surface: A lover declares that, given the right meal, they will do whatever is asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is O, nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a general servant employed to do every kind of job, so one who would say this.

clue.text: Take to Sky, receiving line from the Sun?

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the line goes inside the climbing word

parts.note: to soar is to take to the sky

explanation.surface: A satellite broadcaster takes on a line from a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest Sky television and the Sun newspaper; here they are just the sky and our star.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar is the adjective for anything coming from or relating to the Sun.
